how-much-to-charge.html.text:
← Moving company bid calculator

How much should movers charge for a local move?

Bedroom count is a real-estate number, not a labor number. Two 3-bedroom houses can be a first-floor short carry or a third-floor walk-up with an 80-foot carry to the truck — the same "3BR local move" quote covers both, and one of them is how a Saturday that looked like $900 becomes a loss. Price the walk, not the bedrooms.

Open the free moving bid calculator

What a bedroom-count price cannot see

Stairs. Every flight is extra trips, and extra trips scale with how much you're moving, not a flat per-flight surcharge. A studio up two flights and a four-bedroom house up two flights are not the same stair penalty.

Long carry. Distance from the door to the truck adds time the same way stairs do — more trips at a longer walk, scaled to cubic feet, not a guess.

Packing and drive time. Packing services and the drive between locations are their own clock hours, billed at the same loaded rate as the load and unload.

A bid you can defend

  1. Price load and unload hours from the inventory, not the bedroom count.
  2. Add stair and long-carry hours that scale with cubic feet.
  3. Add packing and drive time as their own hours.
  4. Multiply total hours by crew size and loaded wage, then add truck, fuel, materials, overhead, and margin.

The calculator does that arithmetic in your browser. It is not a recommended price, a tariff, or a guarantee — verify every figure against your own payroll, insurance, and times before sending a bid.

Worked example

Two 3-bedroom houses, same inventory: one is a first-floor unit with a short carry to the curb, the other is a third-floor walk-up with an 80-foot carry to where the truck can park. A flat "3BR local move" quote prices them the same. The stair and long-carry hours the second job actually needs — scaled to the cubic feet being moved, not a flat surcharge per flight — are exactly what turns a comfortable Saturday into a loss if they're missing from the bid. The calculator adds those hours before it prices the job.

Common questions

How do movers price a local job?

From clock hours: load and unload time for the inventory, plus extra hours for stairs and a long carry that scale with cubic feet, plus packing and drive time. Hours times crew size times loaded wage, then truck, fuel, materials, overhead, and margin.

Why can't I bid a move by bedroom count?

Two 3-bedroom houses can be a first-floor short carry or a third-floor walk-up with an 80-foot carry. Bedroom count cannot see the extra trips. That is how a Saturday that looked like $900 becomes a loss.

How much extra should stairs add to a moving quote?

Stairs add trips, so the extra hours should scale with how much you are moving, not a flat surcharge. This tool starts from minutes per flight per 200 cubic feet and lets you replace that with a time from your own crew.

Is this the price I should charge?

No. The output is arithmetic on the numbers you entered. It is not a recommended price, a tariff, or a guarantee. Verify every figure against your own payroll, insurance, and times before sending a bid.

It is not legal, tax, financial, or business advice, and it does not replace a qualified professional. vs-a-bedroom-count-quote.html.text:
← Moving Company Bid Calculator

This calculator vs. a bedroom-count quote

“3 bedroom house — $1,035” is not a price for a move — it is a price for one specific access situation, quietly applied to every house of that size that calls in.

What a bedroom-count quote is

A bedroom-count quote is the fastest way to estimate: match the house to a size bracket and read off a price. Customers shop it because it is easy to compare between movers, and it is the number a customer holding a competitor's online estimate will ask you to match.

The number behind it was set for one job — first-floor or elevator access, no long carry to the truck — and then reused for every house of that size afterward, whether or not the next house looks anything like the one the quote was built on.

What this calculator is

This page keeps no account and sends nothing to a server. You enter a room-by-room inventory (cubic feet and clock hours per room or item), stairs at pickup and drop-off, the longest carry from door to truck, elevator wait, packing and drive time, plus your own crew wage and cost figures. It prices access hours from the inventory's volume — more cubic feet, more stair and carry trips — then returns the walk-away price and a bid price above your target margin — for this job, not a generic one.

What a bedroom-count quote doesWhat this calculator does instead
Charges the same price whether the house is first-floor or a third-floor walk-up — even though a walk-up alone can add several hours of stair trips to the same inventory. Prices stairs at pickup and drop-off from the inventory's volume, so a walk-up is never quoted off a first-floor rate.
Has no line for a long carry from the door to the truck, regardless of whether it is 20 feet or 150 feet. Prices carry distance from the inventory's volume, so a long carry costs more than a driveway drop-off on the same house.
Prices the house by a size bracket, with no separate line for elevator wait the whole crew sits through once per stop. Prices elevator wait as its own clock-hour line, on top of stairs and carry.
Gives the crew a number to quote, not a number to check a quote against. Reports the walk-away price and the dollar gap against what a bedroom-count quote would have charged the same house, so a shopped price can be scored against real cost before you commit to it.

Two houses, the same access-blind quote

Using this calculator's own shipped presets:

JobThis calculator's priceA flat $1,035.00 bedroom-count quote, applied by inventory aloneGap
3 bedroom house (1,100 cu ft), first floor, no long carry (the job this quote was built on)$1,035.00 (same job, same quote)$1,035.00 (same job, same quote)No gap: this is the one job the quote fits.
Same 3 bedroom house, third-floor walk-up at drop-off, 150 ft carry to the truck$1,491.59 bid price; $1,193.27 break-even cost$1,035.00The bedroom-count quote charges $158.27 below this job's own break-even cost — before a dollar of profit — and $456.59 below the calculator's bid price.

Both rows price the identical 1,100 cu ft, 5-clock-hour inventory. Only the access changes: three flights of stairs at drop-off and a 150-foot carry add 3.85 hours the bedroom-count quote never sees. Run your own house's numbers in the calculator to see where it falls.

A bedroom-count quote is not wrong because it is simple — it is wrong when it is applied outside the one access situation it was built for, and nothing about a size-bracket number tells you when that has happened. This calculator does not know your local market; it replaces the arithmetic a bedroom-count quote skips.

Common questions

Why does a bedroom-count quote get a moving job wrong?

Because the cost driver is access, not room count. A third-floor walk-up with a long carry to the truck needs many more trips per cubic foot moved than a first-floor unit of the same size -- stairs and long carries scale with how much furniture has to make the trip, not with the number of bedrooms. A bedroom-count quote charges both the same because it only ever looked at inventory.

What does a bedroom-count quote usually leave out entirely?

Stairs, long carries, and elevator wait. A quote built from "how many bedrooms" has no line for any of them -- it is a number for a first-floor, short-carry load, reused for every access situation afterward, including a walk-up that turns the same furniture into several extra trips.

How big is the pricing gap in practice?

On this calculator's own shipped presets: a 3-bedroom house (1,100 cu ft) on the first floor with no long carry prices at $1,035.00. Applying that same $1,035.00 quote to the identical 3-bedroom inventory on a third-floor walk-up with a 150-foot carry to the truck quotes $1,035.00 against that job's own $1,193.27 break-even cost -- $158.27 below break-even, before a dollar of profit, and $456.59 below the calculator's own bid price.

Is a bedroom-count quote ever the right way to quote?

For a narrow band of near-identical jobs -- same inventory, first floor or an elevator both times, no long carry either time -- a bedroom-count quote can land close. The risk is applying it outside that band without noticing, because the quote does not know which access situation it was built on and neither does the mover until the stairs and carry are actually walked.

Does this calculator know what moving costs in my market?

No. It has no data on local labor rates or truck costs. It takes the room-by-room inventory, stairs, long carry, elevator wait, packing and drive time, plus the crew wage and cost figures you enter, and turns that into a price for this job -- the arithmetic a bedroom-count quote skips, not a market survey.

vs-smartmoving.html.text:
← Moving Company Bid Calculator

This calculator vs. SmartMoving

Two different shapes: SmartMoving is all-in-one CRM, dispatch, estimating, and billing software for running a moving company. This page is a free, private worksheet for one question — what should this local move cost, given its inventory, stairs, and long carry, before you open a business-management system.

What each tool is for

SmartMoving is all-in-one software built specifically for moving companies, founded in 2018 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas. It combines CRM and lead management, online booking, dispatch and job scheduling, estimating, digital signatures, storage management, billing, reporting, and a customer portal into one subscription system, with integrations into QuickBooks and Mailchimp for accounting and marketing. SmartMoving says thousands of moving companies run their business on it, and it made the 2024 Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies. It also took a growth investment from Mainsail Partners, a growth-equity firm. SmartMoving's own pricing page is not reachable from this session to confirm today's exact plan names or dollar figures, so no price for it is invented here: only its well-documented identity and category — all-in-one moving-company business software, sold as a subscription account — are stated, and no dollar amount for SmartMoving appears on this page.

This calculator does none of what SmartMoving does. It does not manage leads, online booking, dispatch across a fleet, storage, or billing, and it stores no customer or job record on a server. It takes one local move's room-by-room inventory — cubic feet and clock hours per room or specialty item — plus stairs, a long carry, elevator wait, packing and drive time, crew wage, payroll burden, truck, fuel, materials, overhead, and target margin, and turns that into the crew hours the job actually consumes, the price per cubic foot, the effective hourly rate per mover, and the walk-away price below which the job loses money — plus, if you already have a bedroom-count quote on the table, a check of whether it clears that walk-away floor, and a single printable customer proposal for that one job. It runs free in any browser, keeps no account, and uploads nothing you type. It prices one local move; it does not handle long-distance tariffs or storage-in-transit.

Most moving companies get different value from each: SmartMoving (or a comparable moving-company platform) for running leads, booking, dispatch, storage, and billing across a whole company as an ongoing subscription, and a private calculator like this one for an instant, no-login gut-check on what one local move should cost from its inventory and access before a business system is involved. This page's own figures are a pricing model, not a signed proposal, an invoice, or a walk-through.

This tool needs no account and no sign-in: it is a static page, the arithmetic runs in your browser, and once it has loaded it keeps working with the connection off.

Common questions

Should I use this calculator or SmartMoving?

They do different jobs, and a moving company of any size will likely end up touching both eventually. SmartMoving is all-in-one software for moving companies, founded in 2018 and headquartered in Dallas, Texas, combining CRM, lead management, online booking, dispatch and job scheduling, estimating, digital signatures, storage management, billing, and a customer portal into one subscription system, with QuickBooks and Mailchimp integrations. It says thousands of moving companies run on it, and it made the 2024 Inc. 5000 list of fastest-growing private companies. It is sold as an ongoing subscription account. This calculator does one narrower thing: starting from a room-by-room inventory with cubic feet and clock hours, plus stairs, a long carry, elevator wait, packing and drive time, crew wage, payroll burden, truck, fuel, materials, overhead, and target margin, it turns that into the crew hours the job actually consumes, the price per cubic foot, the effective hourly rate per mover, and the walk-away price below which the job loses money, before any of it touches a business-management system. It runs free in any browser, keeps no account, and uploads nothing you type. A moving company that already manages leads, dispatch, storage, and billing across every crew and every job is better served by SmartMoving or a comparable moving-company platform; a mover who wants an instant, private gut-check on what one local job should cost from its stairs and carry before opening a business system is in the right place here.
